sections.title: What marketing management covers here
sections.content:
Marketing management is the standing work of running your marketing operation rather than a project with an end date. It covers implementing and maintaining HubSpot, building the automation that moves people through it, and running the campaigns that fill it. We act as an extension of your team, which in practice means your marketing meeting has somebody in it who is accountable for the platform and the content at the same time.

Most teams buy these separately and then spend their attention on the seam. An agency configures a workflow, a different agency writes the emails inside it, and the person who has to make those two things agree is you.

sections.title: HubSpot implementation and cleanup
sections.content: Portal setup, migration, and the unglamorous work of making an existing portal usable. Properties that mean something, lifecycle stages that match how you sell, lists that are not quietly stale, and reporting you trust enough to act on. Plenty of this work is cleanup rather than implementation, because the portal was set up correctly for a business that has since changed.

sections.title: Marketing automation
sections.content: The workflows that route a lead, score it, hand it to sales, and follow up when nobody does. Automation fails in two ordinary ways, either nothing is built or too much is built and no one remembers what fires when. We document what exists before adding to it, and we turn off what is running for no reason.

sections.title: Campaign management
sections.content: Planning, building, and running campaigns end to end, with the writing included rather than subcontracted. A campaign is a landing page, a form, a sequence, a set of social posts, and reporting that says whether it worked, and every one of those is content somebody has to produce.

sections.title: White-label for agencies
sections.content: All of it is available white-label. Agencies bring us in as their marketing operations team and the work goes out under their logo, with their client relationship untouched. If that is the shape you need, the agency track has its own page.

If marketing management is not the piece you are missing, these are the neighboring pages.

  • All services is the full picture of what we write and run.
  • Email Marketing is the lifecycle work on its own, without the platform engagement around it.
  • Pricing is public, so you can size this before you talk to anybody.

items.question: Do we need to be on HubSpot?
items.answer: For the platform work, yes, that is what we run. The campaign and content work does not depend on it, and we will say so if HubSpot is the wrong tool for what you are trying to do.

items.question: Can you take over a portal somebody else built?
items.answer: That is most of what we do. We audit what is there, document the workflows nobody can explain, and turn off what is firing for no reason before we add anything.

items.question: Is the content included or separate?
items.answer: Included. The reason to buy marketing management from a content company is that the emails, pages, and posts inside the workflows get written by the same team that built them.

items.question: Can this go out under our agency's name?
items.answer: Yes. White-label is available across the engagement, and your client relationship stays yours.
